name: MAPE-K Feedback Loop
description: Organize runtime adaptation around Monitor, Analyze, Plan, and Execute activities that share knowledge.
benefits: provides clear locations for monitoring, diagnosis, planning, and execution
tradeoffs: control-loop latency may affect adaptation speed
constraints: runtime monitoring must be available
effectors must expose approved adaptation actions
provenance_note: The feedback-loop concept is grounded in autonomic computing and architecture-based self-adaptation literature.

name: Centralized Adaptation Controller
description: Use one logical controller to coordinate runtime adaptation decisions for the managed system.
benefits: makes policy enforcement easier to inspect
tradeoffs: may scale poorly for highly distributed systems
constraints: controller must remain available
runtime state must be observable from the controller
provenance_note: Centralized external adaptation control is represented using architecture-based self-adaptation literature.

name: Decentralized Adaptation Control
description: Distribute adaptation responsibilities among multiple coordinating controllers or agents.
applicability: systems without a single global controller
tradeoffs: global safety enforcement becomes more complex
constraints: controllers require coordination mechanisms
consistency requirements must be defined
provenance_note: Decentralized control is included as an explicit architecture-design alternative in this demonstrator. No specific literature source is claimed for the exact entry as currently written.

name: Architectural Knowledge Retrieval
description: Retrieve relevant architectural knowledge before asking an LLM to reason about architecture design decisions.
benefits: grounds architectural reasoning in an explicit knowledge source
allows retrieved evidence to be inspected
tradeoffs: irrelevant knowledge may bias architectural decisions
constraints: retrieved knowledge must remain advisory
important design constraints must be represented explicitly
provenance_note: RAG is literature-grounded, while its application to the curated software-architecture knowledge workflow is a research-specific design decision.

name: LLM Architecture Reasoning Component
description: Use an LLM for requirement interpretation, architectural alternative generation, trade-off explanation, and rationale generation.
tradeoffs: outputs may be incorrect or inconsistent
architectural decisions cannot be accepted without validation
constraints: LLM output must not be treated as authoritative
important decisions require validation and human approval
provenance_note: LLM support for architectural reasoning and for self-adaptive-system reasoning is supported by the cited empirical and exploratory literature.

name: Deterministic Safety Gate
description: Place a deterministic policy-validation component between AI-generated adaptation plans and system effectors.
benefits: prevents known policy violations from reaching effectors
separates generative reasoning from trusted enforcement
tradeoffs: incorrect rules may reject useful plans
cannot guarantee properties outside encoded constraints
constraints: hard constraints must be machine-checkable
all executable plans must pass through the safety gate
provenance_note: The exact deterministic gate separating generative reasoning from effector authority is a safety boundary defined by this research architecture.

name: Horizontal Resource Scaling
description: Add or remove computational resources in response to workload and utilization changes.
benefits: reduces unnecessary resources when demand falls
tradeoffs: new resources may require startup time
constraints: minimum and maximum resource bounds should be explicit
resource startup state should be monitored
provenance_note: Horizontal server scaling is directly relevant to the SWIM exemplar and its adaptation space.

name: Feature Degradation Through Dimmer Control
description: Temporarily reduce optional functionality to protect critical response-time goals during constrained conditions.
benefits: reduces workload without completely denying service
tradeoffs: quality experienced by users may decline
constraints: optional and mandatory functionality must be distinguishable
dimmer bounds must be explicit
provenance_note: Dimmer-based optional-content degradation is grounded in the SWIM exemplar's adaptation mechanisms.

name: Models at Runtime
description: Maintain runtime representations of relevant system, environment, goals, or adaptation knowledge that can support reasoning during execution.
benefits: supports reasoning about current system state
can connect runtime observations to adaptation decisions
constraints: runtime models must remain sufficiently synchronized with the managed system
provenance_note: The use of explicit runtime models is grounded in Models@run.time literature.

name: Runtime Adaptation Memory
description: Store previous adaptation states, decisions, safety verdicts, and observed outcomes for later retrieval.
benefits: allows previous adaptation experience to inform later decisions
supports inspection of prior decisions and outcomes
can distinguish successful and partially successful actions
constraints: current trusted constraints must override retrieved experience
retrieved experience must not directly trigger effectors
provenance_note: Agent memory and experience reuse have literature support, while the exact episode schema and retrieval behavior are specific to this prototype.

name: Bounded Replanning
description: Allow an agent to reconsider failed plans but enforce a maximum number of autonomous recovery attempts.
tradeoffs: retry bounds may terminate before a feasible plan is found
constraints: retry limit must be explicit
each revised plan must be safety-checked again
provenance_note: Agentic replanning is literature-informed, while the explicit bounded-retry authority rule is a research-design decision of this architecture.

name: Human Approval and Escalation
description: Keep humans responsible for final design-time architecture approval and provide an escalation point when autonomous runtime recovery cannot find an acceptable plan.
benefits: preserves human authority over architectural decisions
provides a fallback when autonomous recovery is exhausted
tradeoffs: human involvement may increase decision latency
operator availability may be required in deployed systems
constraints: the prototype must distinguish real human interaction from simulated escalation
provenance_note: Human involvement is literature-supported, while the exact division of design-time approval and runtime escalation authority is explicitly defined by this research.

name: Post-Execution Validation
description: Observe the managed system after an adaptation action and compare the actual effect against the intended goal.
benefits: distinguishes proposed actions from observed effects
supports PASS, PARTIAL, and FAIL outcome semantics
provides evidence for future adaptation memory
tradeoffs: effects may take time to become observable
constraints: outcomes should be based on observed state rather than assumed action success
provenance_note: Closed-loop observation after adaptation is literature-grounded; the exact PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL outcome semantics are research-specific.

name: Architecture Decision Record
description: Record an architectural decision together with its context, considered alternatives, selected option, rationale, and consequences.
constraints: generated rationale must correspond to the actual selected architecture
provenance_note: The project deliberately uses an ADR-style artifact for traceability. No external ADR source is claimed by the current provenance registry.

name: Weighted Quality-Attribute Trade-off Analysis
description: Evaluate candidate architectures against explicit quality attributes using architect-defined weights and explain the trade-offs rather than selecting solely from an LLM preference.
benefits: allows architects to inspect how priorities affect ranking
tradeoffs: numeric scores simplify complex architectural judgments
results depend on selected criteria and weights
constraints: weights must be explicitly documented
scores require rationale
the highest numerical score must not automatically bypass architect validation
provenance_note: Architecture quality-attribute trade-off analysis is literature-grounded. The prototype's 1-to-5 scoring and architect-defined weighted-total calculation are a research-specific decision-support mechanism and are not claimed to be ATAM.
